# nearcache

```go
import "github.com/eugeneliukindev/gashe/backend/nearcache"
```

Package nearcache is a two\-level gashe.Backend: a small cache in process memory in front of a shared backend such as Redis. Hot keys are read from memory, so they do not load one Redis node, and reads keep working for a while when the shared backend is slow.

<a name="Backend"></a>
## type [Backend](<https://github.com/eugeneliukindev/gashe/blob/main/backend/nearcache/nearcache.go#L45-L54>)

Backend reads through local, then shared; writes and deletes go to shared and drop the local copy. Locks, counters and TTLs always use shared.

```go
type Backend struct {
    // contains filtered or unexported fields
}
```

<a name="New"></a>
### func [New](<https://github.com/eugeneliukindev/gashe/blob/main/backend/nearcache/nearcache.go#L83>)

```go
func New(local, shared gashe.Backend, o Options) *Backend
```

New returns a near cache Backend. local is usually a memory.Backend, shared a Redis backend; both are owned by the caller, and Close closes neither. With a Bus, New starts listening to it and Close stops. It panics on a negative LocalTTL.

<details><summary>Example</summary>
<p>



```go
package main

import (
	"context"
	"fmt"
	"time"

	"github.com/eugeneliukindev/gashe"
	"github.com/eugeneliukindev/gashe/backend/memory"
	"github.com/eugeneliukindev/gashe/backend/nearcache"
)

func main() {
	ctx := context.Background()
	local := memory.New(memory.Options{MaxEntries: 100})
	defer local.Close()
	shared := memory.New(memory.Options{}) // usually Redis
	defer shared.Close()
	near := nearcache.New(local, shared, nearcache.Options{LocalTTL: time.Minute})
	defer func() { _ = near.Close() }()
	c := gashe.New(near, gashe.Options{})

	_ = c.Set(ctx, "user:42", "Ann", time.Hour) // goes to shared
	var name string
	_ = c.Get(ctx, "user:42", &name) // copies the value to local
	fmt.Println(name, local.Len(), shared.Len())

	_, _ = shared.Delete(ctx, "user:42") // as another process without a Bus would
	_ = c.Get(ctx, "user:42", &name)     // still answered from local for up to LocalTTL
	fmt.Println(name)
}
```

#### Output

```
Ann 1 1
Ann
```

<a name="Bus"></a>
## type [Bus](<https://github.com/eugeneliukindev/gashe/blob/main/backend/nearcache/nearcache.go#L35-L41>)

Bus carries "these keys changed" messages between the near caches of all processes. Only key names travel; a process that needs the new value reads it from the shared backend.

```go
type Bus interface {
    // Publish tells the other processes that keys changed. nil means every key.
    Publish(ctx context.Context, keys []string) error
    // Subscribe calls changed with the keys other processes published, and changed(nil) whenever
    // messages may have been lost, such as after a reconnect. It returns when ctx is done.
    Subscribe(ctx context.Context, changed func(keys []string)) error
}
```

<a name="Options"></a>
## type [Options](<https://github.com/eugeneliukindev/gashe/blob/main/backend/nearcache/nearcache.go#L22-L31>)

Options configures a near cache Backend.

```go
type Options struct {
    // LocalTTL is how long a value read from the shared backend is kept in memory. It is also how
    // long another process may keep answering with a value this process already changed.
    // 0 means 5 seconds.
    LocalTTL time.Duration
    // Bus, when set, tells the near caches of other processes which keys this one changed, so they
    // drop their copies at once instead of after LocalTTL. backend/redis provides one over
    // pub/sub. nil means other processes see a change only after LocalTTL.
    Bus Bus
}
```
